title: MacConkey Agar

references.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

purpose: Selects for Gram-negative enteric bacteria while inhibiting most Gram-positive organisms, and differentiates lactose-fermenting from non-lactose-fermenting Gram-negative organisms.

reference.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

preparationSummary: Suspend the dehydrated powder per the manufacturer's stated concentration, heat with agitation to boiling to fully dissolve, then sterilize and pour while still liquid.

sterilization.value: commonly autoclaved at 121°C for 15 minutes; avoid prolonged overheating, which can degrade the indicator/carbohydrate

storage: Refrigerate prepared plates in sealed bags, protected from light (crystal violet and neutral red are light-sensitive over time).
expectedAppearance: Translucent to slightly opaque agar with a pink-red tint from neutral red before inoculation.
qualityControl: Verify selectivity (a Gram-positive control such as Staphylococcus aureus should be inhibited) and differentiation (a known lactose fermenter should turn pink/red; a non-fermenter should remain colorless) against reference organisms.

reactions.organismOrGroup: Lactose-fermenting Gram-negative rods (e.g. many E. coli strains)
reactions.reaction: Pink to red colonies, sometimes with a surrounding precipitate, due to acid production lowering pH and shifting the neutral red indicator

reactions.organismOrGroup: Non-lactose-fermenting Gram-negative rods (e.g. many Salmonella, Shigella strains)

manufacturerNotes: Bile salt and dye concentrations vary somewhat between manufacturers and between 'MacConkey Agar' and 'MacConkey Agar without crystal violet' variants — confirm the exact product formulation before relying on selectivity claims.
